findings.title: No incident-response documentation, severity taxonomy, roles, or postmortem process exists anywhere in the repository
evidence: git ls-files '*.md' - tracked docs are only AGENTS.md, README.md, docs/{CONTROL_PLANE,DATA,FUTURE_WORK,METHODOLOGY,PHASE_TIMINGS}.md plus audit/example result markdown; no INCIDENT/RUNBOOK/SECURITY/ONCALL file
git ls-files filtered for incident|runbook|postmortem|oncall|disaster|tabletop|breach - zero matches
README.md:170-203 - describes the benchd control plane and operator surface with no incident/rollback/escalation section
docs/CONTROL_PLANE.md:214-254 - 'Operating notes' cover staleness/reaper/token rotation mechanics but define no incident roles, severities, containment, comms or postmortem
findings.impact: Operators of a control plane that can remotely reboot/shut down machines, run arbitrary shell (exec/shell) and raw-write block devices (iso_write/iso_write_slot) have no agreed roles, severity scale, containment steps, communication plan or postmortem template; incident handling is ad hoc and untrainable.
findings.recommendation: Add docs/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md defining severity (SEV1-4), roles (incident commander/comms/scribe), containment/escalation, and a comms + blameless-postmortem template; link it from README and AGENTS.md and run the scenarios in this report as a tabletop.

findings.title: No monitoring or alerting: failures are only visible when a human watches the web dashboard
evidence: server/benchd.py:629-634 - GET /health returns only {ok,time,git,version,protocol,latest,runners}; liveness, not alertable signal
server/benchd.py:718-719 - GET /api/v1/metrics returns a static METRICS catalogue (server/benchd.py:78-90), not a Prometheus scrape endpoint
docs/CONTROL_PLANE.md:130 - '/metrics - the metric catalogue (key -> label)'
docs/CONTROL_PLANE.md:273-278 - Roadmap lists 'Prometheus//metrics export and alerting (throttle, TDR, over-temp)' as future work
grep for alert|webhook|notify|slack|email|pagerduty across the repo - no notification/alerting code
docs/CONTROL_PLANE.md:222-223 - runners are only marked offline after 15 s with no push/alert; observability is pull-only in the UI
findings.impact: Runner death, a failed/aborted overnight run, server disk pressure, unbounded SQLite growth (benchd.py:254 'grows ~1 row/second per active run'), and over-temp/throttle conditions are never surfaced - someone must be staring at the Live tab. A total loss of the monitoring path itself (benchd process, its host, or the DB) is undetected and unalerted.
findings.recommendation: Add a Prometheus text /metrics endpoint plus alert rules (runner offline > 60s, run failed, GPU over-temp/throttle bit set, server disk < 10%, DB size/inode growth), or at minimum a webhook/email fired on run-failed and runner-offline events; add a heartbeat watch that alerts if benchd itself stops.

findings.title: No backup or restore procedure for the control-plane SQLite database (all fleet history, artifacts and per-runner keys)
evidence: server/benchd.py:50 - DEFAULT_DB = server/data/benchd.sqlite is the single authoritative store
server/benchd.py:94-143 - schema holds runners (incl. api_key), runs, phases, telemetry, logs, commands, events, artifacts, schedules
server/benchd.py:154 - WAL mode with synchronous=NORMAL
.gitignore:26-28 - server/data/ and server/benchd.conf are git-ignored, so the DB is not versioned or captured anywhere
git ls-files - no backup/restore script for the DB; docs/CONTROL_PLANE.md:254 only notes WAL growth, no backup/RPO/RTO
findings.impact: Loss of the DB file (host failure, disk full, an accidental operator DELETE at server/benchd.py:665-672) is unrecoverable: run history, attached artifacts, schedules and every per-runner API key are gone, forcing re-registration of the whole fleet. There is no documented recovery time or recovery point objective.
findings.recommendation: Ship a backup script using `sqlite3 data/benchd.sqlite '.backup'` on a schedule with retention, document a tested restore runbook and RPO/RTO, and record the last successful restore test as evidence; add an alert on backup failure.

findings.title: No operator audit log: privileged commands and destructive deletes carry no actor identity or durable trail
evidence: server/benchd.py:119-122 - commands table stores id/runner_id/run_id/kind/payload/status/created/sent/acked/result - no actor/operator column
server/benchd.py:1220-1232 - _issue_command records only kind+payload; the shared token means every operator is indistinguishable (server/benchd.py:14-17, README.md:359)
server/benchd.py:653-681 - do_DELETE removes run rows plus their phases/telemetry/events/artifacts (lines 665-672) and runner rows (673-680) with no audit trail
server/benchd.py:515-525 - the only logging redacts token= but persists nothing; no actor, no retention
docs/CONTROL_PLANE.md:273-275 - Roadmap: 'Operator logins (per-user accounts) instead of the shared join token' (unimplemented)
findings.impact: After a destructive action (iso_write to the wrong device, reboot/shutdown of a busy host, exec, or deletion of a run/runner) there is no way to attribute it. Admin abuse or an honest mistake cannot be investigated or reconstructed from the evidence.
findings.recommendation: Add an append-only audit table (ts, actor, source address, action kind, target runner/run, payload summary, result) written by every operator-only route, retain it independently of run deletion, and implement per-user operator accounts (roadmap) so the actor is identifiable.

findings.title: No data-breach or vulnerability-disclosure process, while a public repo bakes a world-readable operator token into ISO/app artifacts
evidence: git ls-files - no SECURITY.md or responsible-disclosure/breach process file

README.md:158-163 - CI bakes the BENCH_AGENT_CONF control-plane token into each public app bundle; README.md:359-363 - repo and ISO releases are public, 'a token baked into an ISO is world-readable; rotate it if a stick leaves the lab'
.github/workflows/build-iso.yml:62-82 - writes the BENCH_AGENT_CONF / BENCH_UPLOAD_CONF secrets into the image
AGENTS.md:178-186 - acknowledges the public repo + baked-token exposure but defines no breach/rotation procedure
findings.impact: If a stick/bundle leaks, there is no documented breach path: who is notified, which log/artifact proves the exposure, how the token and per-runner keys are rotated, and how the fleet is verified clean. The operator token also grants reboot/shutdown/exec across the fleet, so an undetected leaked token is a high-impact scenario.
findings.recommendation: Add SECURITY.md (private disclosure contact/SLA) and a breach-response checklist including mandatory token + per-runner-key rotation, artifact/DB impact assessment, and post-rotation verification; reference it from README/AGENTS.md.

findings.title: Prior audit findings are all still marked open and were never re-verified, so the same incident class recurs
evidence: docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/follow_up_register.md:5-11 - all 7 findings (incl. SUPPLY-P1-001) status 'open' with no re-verification date or owner closure
bench/Get-Sensors.ps1:13-22 - still downloads '.../releases/latest/download/LibreHardwareMonitor.zip' and Add-Type loads it with no checksum/signature check (the same defect SUPPLY-P1-001 describes)
bench/Sample-Sensors.ps1:36-58 - same unpinned 'releases/latest' plus a mutable master-branch fallback, still unverified at the current commit
findings.impact: There is no recurrence tracking: a previously-identified supply-chain incident class (unverified download loaded in-process) is still live, and the follow-up register gives no signal that fixes were attempted, landed or stuck.
findings.recommendation: Add re-verification dates and closure evidence to the follow-up register, pin LibreHardwareMonitor to a specific release with a committed SHA-256 verified before Expand-Archive/Add-Type (fail closed), and add a regression test asserting the pinned URL/hash so the finding cannot silently reopen.
